featured_reviews.name: Hemant Desai
featured_reviews.review_text: We recently visited Hodi restaurant, a newly opened restaurant in Mulund East, which specializes in non-vegetarian cuisine with a focus on seafood, it also has a vegetarian menu. Although their menu primarily caters to seafood lovers, we opted to try their chicken and mutton dishes. Unfortunately, the taste was average, with the mutton having an unusual flavor that might be attributed to improper cleaning or preparation. The paya soup was overly sour. Additionally, we found the prices to be on the higher side. However, considering the limited options for non-vegetarian family restaurants in Mulund East, Hodi could be a viable choice for those craving non-veg cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Amey Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Hodi Seafood Restaurant with family and had a generally nice experience.

The highlights of our meal were definitely the Crab Soup and Crab Lollipops—both were delicious and packed with flavor. The Paya Soup was equally impressive and comforting. For starters, the Prawns Kurkure provided a great crunch and the Wade were absolutely awesome and perfect with the meal.

On the downside, the Chicken Lollipop and Teesrya (Clams) Gravy were just "ok ok"—they didn't quite hit the mark for us and we didn't enjoy them as much as the other dishes.

Overall, it’s a lovely spot for a family outing with some standout seafood items. Must try for the crab dishes and Wade!

featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sindhudurg Family Dining to celebrate a birthday, and overall it was a mixed experience.

The restaurant is very conveniently located, especially for people coming from Mulund East railway station. The management is also supportive for small celebrations like birthdays, so that’s a plus.

However, the space is quite compact with tight seating. It can feel a bit congested, and there’s definitely room for improvement in terms of space management and comfort.

Service is another area that needs attention. There was noticeable delay in serving orders, and it seemed to be a common issue across tables, not just ours.

Coming to food:

Starters like Bombil Fry, Crab Lollipop, and Chicken Tikka Kebab were good in taste. The Crab Lollipop was the highlight.

We tried Rawas and Surmai Thalis. Surmai was fresh and tasty, while Rawas was just average. The fish curry in the thali was quite bland.

Prawns Malvani Masala and Pomfret Tawa Fry were disappointing. The prawns dish had an overpowering coconut taste, and the pomfret didn’t feel very fresh.

Chicken Sukha was flavorful and well-prepared, but Kombdi Vade didn’t feel authentic—it was more like a puri.

Surmai Tawa Fry (ordered later) was again very good.

Solkadhi was impressive and better than many nearby seafood places.

One more thing to note is the portion size—it felt a bit less for the price, so overall it came across as slightly expensive for the quantity served.

Overall, it’s a decent place for seafood with some really good dishes, but consistency, authenticity, service speed, and portion sizing need improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malvan Tadka in Mulund offers a fairly comfortable introduction to coastal cuisine, though the overall experience leans more toward a North Indian palate than an authentically bold Malvani one. The food is decent and satisfying in parts, but if you’re expecting deeply robust, coconut-forward, fiery coastal gravies, you may find the flavours slightly toned down and more mainstream.

Over multiple visits, we’ve tried a wide range of their menu. The Surmai Fry remains one of the better choices — fresh, nicely marinated, and well cooked. The Pomfret Fry, Bangda Fry, and Bombil Fry are competently done, while the Stuffed Bombil Fry stands out as one of the more memorable dishes — flavourful and prepared with care. Seafood combinations featuring Kolambi Masala, prawn preparations, and even seasonal Crab Masala offer variety, though the gravies sometimes feel milder than traditional Malvani spice profiles.

Among the non-seafood options, the Chicken (Malvani style), Mutton preparations, Chicken Masala, Chicken Sukka, and Mutton Sukka are decent, but again lean toward a safer, more North Indian-style gravy base rather than a distinctly coastal punch. However, the Chicken Gharguti Handi was exceptionally good — homely, balanced, and far more flavourful than expected. It’s easily one of the highlights of the meal.

Accompaniments like Neer Dosa, Bhakri, and Kombdi Vade (when available) pair well with the curries, and the Solkadhi offers a refreshing coastal touch to round off the meal.

Overall, Malvan Tadka delivers average, serviceable food with a few standout dishes like the Chicken Gharguti Handi and Stuffed Bombil Fry elevating the experience. It may not fully satisfy purists seeking strong Malvani authenticity, but for those looking for a milder, more accessible version of coastal cuisine in Mulund, it does an okay job. A balanced three-star experience — pleasant, but not particularly distinctive.

No matter how many years have passed, one thing that has remained beautifully consistent is their authentic Malvani flavour and unmatched freshness of seafood. It’s rare to find a place that maintains such high standards for decades and Sindhudurg has managed to do just that.
Recently, I hosted my mom’s retirement dinner here for her and her colleagues and we had the pleasure of dining in their “baithak” which is a cozy, exclusive space that offers a sense of privacy and warmth. The staff made sure everything ran smoothly, from the service to the presentation. It truly felt personal and thoughtfully managed, just like a home-style feast with restaurant level perfection.
Coming to the food, we ordered a spread that showcased the best of what Sindhudurg has to offer: Prawns Thali, Pomfret Thali, Surmai Thali, Chicken Sukkha Thali, Mutton Sukkha Thali and even one Veg Thali for variety. Every bite took me back to my childhood memories, reminding me why this place is more than just a restaurant, it’s an emotion for anyone who grew up around Thane. Highly recommend it to anyone craving authentic Malvani comfort food served with consistency, warmth and heart.

For food lovers in Thane who enjoy spicy flavors, traditional recipes, and fresh seafood, Hotel Sindhudurg has become a trusted and popular dining destination. The restaurant truly represents the rich coastal food culture of Maharashtra right in the heart of Thane.
The biggest attraction of Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, is its excellent seafood selection. Dishes prepared using fresh fish, prawns, crabs, and other seafood items are the highlights of the menu. The seafood is cooked in traditional Malvani style, using coconut-based gravies, kokum, and strong yet balanced spices. Popular seafood curries are full of flavor and have the perfect level of spiciness that Malvani cuisine is known for. Seafood lovers across Thane often visit the hotel specifically for these dishes.
Apart from seafood, Hotel Sindhudurg in Thane is also famous for its non-vegetarian Maharashtrian dishes. Items like chicken, mutton, and traditional curries are prepared with authentic masalas that give a bold and spicy taste. The food reflects true Maharashtrian spice levels, making it ideal for those who enjoy hot, flavorful meals. Bhakri, rice, and solkadhi served with the food complete the authentic Malvani dining experience.
The taste and consistency at Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, are highly appreciated. The flavors remain the same over time, which builds trust among regular customers. The food is neither overly oily nor artificial in taste, maintaining a homely yet restaurant-style balance. This consistency makes the hotel a favorite spot for families and non-veg food lovers in Thane.
Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained at Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane. The dining area is neat, tables are cleaned regularly, and the overall atmosphere is simple and comfortable. The service staff is polite, attentive, and experienced in handling customer requests, which adds to a pleasant dining experience.
Another positive point is the reasonable pricing. Considering the quality, quantity, and authentic taste of seafood and non-veg dishes, Hotel Sindhudurg in Thane offers good value for money. This makes it a popular choice among working professionals, families, and seafood lovers from different parts of Thane.
Though the restaurant focuses more on food quality than luxury interiors, its simple setup suits the traditional feel of Malvani cuisine. Minor improvements in décor could enhance the ambiance, but the powerful taste of the food remains the main attraction.
In conclusion, Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, is a top choice for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Malvani seafood, spicy Maharashtrian non-veg cuisine, and traditional flavors. For seafood lovers in Thane who appreciate bold spices and coastal recipes, Hotel Sindhudurg is a must-visit restaurant and a true taste of Maharashtra.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this well-known restaurant Nisarga Restuarant, Mulund, reputed for its lip-smacking fish and chicken dishes, for a family dinner. Unfortunately, our experience did not fully meet expectations.

Ambience & Seating

The initial seating arrangement was inconvenient, as the restaurant couldn't immediately provide adjacent tables for our group of eight. We were seated at two opposite-facing tables. However, after some time, the manager arranged an adjacent setup once another family left, which was appreciated.

Service

The service left room for improvement. Our starter was served later than expected, and one of the signature dishes, fish ghassi, was unavailable. Instead, we opted for fish Malvani, which took 15-20 minutes to arrive.

Food Quality

Vegetarian Dishes: Surprisingly, the vegetarian options stole the show. The Manchow soup, spring rolls, and hara bhara kabab were flavorful and arrived promptly. The mix veg gravy and paneer 65 in the main course were well-cooked and delicious.

Non-Vegetarian Dishes: The fish Malvani was decent but lacked the wow factor expected from a restaurant known for its non-veg specialties.

Overall Experience

While the vegetarian dishes impressed, the delays, unavailability of popular items, and initial seating issues took away from the overall experience.

Rating: 3.5/5

Would recommend this place for vegetarian options but with tempered expectations for service and availability of non-veg dishes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic Malvani cuisine that captures the true essence of coastal Maharashtra, Malvan Tadka is definitely a restaurant you must visit. From the moment you step in, the aroma of freshly ground spices, coconut-based gravies, and sizzling seafood instantly transports you to the Konkan coast.

The ambiance is simple yet warm — wooden interiors, coastal décor, and soft Marathi music playing in the background create the perfect setting for a relaxed dining experience. The staff greets you with genuine hospitality and are always ready to help you choose the best dishes based on your taste preferences.

Coming to the food — it’s nothing short of extraordinary. The Surmai Thali and Prawns Curry are absolute highlights, bursting with flavor and perfectly cooked. The Bombil Fry is crispy on the outside and tender inside, while the Tisrya (clams) Masala is rich and spicy, just the way Malvani food should be. Their signature Chicken Sagoti and Mutton Masala are also a must-try for non-seafood lovers. The portions are generous, and the taste is consistent every time you visit.

What truly makes Malvan Tadka special is the balance they maintain — authentic taste, good hygiene, and reasonable pricing. Despite being busy during weekends, the service remains quick and efficient.

Overall, Malvan Tadka offers a complete experience for anyone who loves traditional coastal cuisine. Whether you’re a seafood enthusiast or someone exploring Malvani food for the first time, this restaurant delivers authenticity, flavor, and satisfaction on every plate. Highly recommended for family dinners and group outings!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Nav Gomantak NX is the part of illustrious an a Gomantak restaurant chain with 2 outlets in Thane itself. Now the premise of this restaurant is to make Goan food available for all!

The menu is predominantly Thali (Sea food/Chicken/Mutton/Veg) and ala carte menu designed to make the experience as Goan as possible.

We ordered Prawns fry - which were delicious deep fried prawns served with side of onions and Green chutney sprinkled with chat masala. We ordered sil kadhi which was yummy but a little spicy.

For Main course we ordered Pomfret and Surmai (king fish) thali. The thali had a fry fish, fish curry, Kishnoor aka sukat, Sol kadhi, coconut chutney infused with kokam, rice, salad.

The portion was enough for person with Fish being well cooked and curry being flavourful, with the Kishnoor and chutney, Sol kadhi being fantastic!

We also ordered a dessert Serradura - a Portuguese origin Pudding - from Goa. Its name is Serradura meaning saw dust in Portuguese - a no bake simple pudding made of 4 ingredients. A lovely layered dessert made of biscuits and cream served chilled. A nice touch to the meal end!

A Nav Gomantak a nice budget restaurant for those who wish to try authentic Goan food!

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Bhattacharjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic Marathi Seafood Experience in Thane | Premium but Worth Trying

Recently visited Gomantak with friends and had a fantastic dining experience. If you are someone who loves authentic Maharashtrian coastal cuisine, especially seafood, this place is definitely worth visiting.

Food Quality & Taste

The biggest highlight of our meal was the Surmai Fry and Pomfret Fry. Both were fresh, flavourful, and cooked perfectly. The fish quality was excellent, nicely marinated, and served with authentic coastal style taste. You can immediately tell they focus on freshness and traditional preparation.

Apart from that, every dish served on our table was impressive. From starters to main course, the taste remained consistently good. Proper homemade-style Marathi flavours with restaurant-level presentation.

Authentic Coastal Feel

This is one of those places where you genuinely get the feel of real Konkan / Marathi non-veg cuisine rather than over-commercialized food. Seafood lovers will definitely appreciate the menu here.

Service & Atmosphere

The restaurant had a lively and family-friendly atmosphere. Staff was courteous, attentive, and service was smooth even with a busy crowd. Food was served properly and overall dining experience felt comfortable.

Pricing

Our total bill came to around ₹5000, which is definitely on the expensive side. So this may not be an everyday dining place for many people. However, considering the seafood quality, taste, and overall experience, it can still feel worth it for special occasions or outings.

Final Verdict

If you are in Thane and looking for authentic Marathi seafood with premium quality, Gomantak is a great choice. Fresh fish, excellent flavours, and satisfying overall experience. Recommended for seafood lovers, family dinners, and those who appreciate traditional taste.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Panigrahi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Nav Gomantak last Saturday. There was a waiting time of around 20 minutes, which is expected given its popularity, especially on weekends.

Javla Masala Papad – Nice start, fresh and well-seasoned
Crab Lollipop – Good, flavourful and well-fried
Fish Finger – Good, crispy and enjoyable
Bharlela Bombil – Okay, slightly underwhelming compared to expectations
Tawa Fry Prawns – Yummy! Easily one of the best dishes of the meal
Pomfret Thali – Good, well-balanced and satisfying
Surmai Thali – Good, fish cooked nicely with authentic flavours
Chicken Xacuti Thali – Great! Rich, aromatic gravy and the standout dish overall

Overall:
Nav Gomantak continues to deliver authentic Malvani/Goan flavours. While a couple of dishes were average, the seafood and chicken preparations largely impressed. Worth the wait if you enjoy traditional coastal cuisine.

Verdict: A solid place for seafood lovers, especially for prawns, surmai, and chicken xacuti. 👍

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
Two areas of improvement would be allowing customers to choose two different mocktails under the offer, especially since all mocktails are priced the same.

Another thing to improve is the coordination between staff members—there was a noticeable communication gap while placing our order.

Visited The Food Studio near Nahur Railway Station and had a generally pleasant experience. We were seated within 5 minutes, and the ambiance was nice with a large TV setup in the center, adding a lively vibe to the place.

We started with French fries and a few starters: Jhinga Koliwada, Makhmali Kumbh, Pomfret Tandoori, and Chicken Burnt Garlic. The Jhinga Koliwada was the highlight—crispy and flavorful. Makhmali Kumbh is a great vegetarian option, stuffed with cheese and tasted quite good. However, the Pomfret Tandoori didn’t meet expectations—the masala lacked punch.

For the main course, we ordered Sabzi Peshawari with roti. It leaned towards the sweeter side, possibly due to the mix of paneer, mushrooms, and green peas. Not bad if you enjoy mildly sweet gravies.

We also tried the mocktail Mulokai under their Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer. The taste was average.

Overall, a good experience with room for a few improvements.
